speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you have a history of a painful, swollen left ankle that resolved on its own, and now you are experiencing increasing pain and swelling in your right knee along with episodes of painful urination. To understand what is going on, have you noticed any fever, chills, or redness in your joints or genital area?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing increasing pain and swelling in his right knee for the past 12 days. He reports pain with urination for the past 3 weeks and had a swollen, painful left ankle joint that resolved on its own about a week ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and using condoms inconsistently. He also reveals that his mother has rheumatoid arthritis. The patient appears anxious.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Reactive arthritis (Reiter's syndrome) secondary to a prior Chlamydia trachomatis infection.

The clinical triad of asymmetric oligoarthritis (left ankle then right knee), urethritis (painful urination), and your history of inconsistent condom use with multiple partners is highly suggestive of reactive arthritis. I need to confirm the infectious etiology and assess joint inflammation.

REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis, Urine NAAT for Chlamydia and Gonorrhea, Rheumatoid Factor, HLA-B27, and CBC.
REQUEST IMAGES: Right knee X-ray and Right knee Ultrasound.
